disputed.question: (b) maxTimeMS 1 on a find whose cursor is fully consumed: code and codeName?
disputed.reason: The managed observations are recorded correctly. The find command itself fails with code 50 ExceededTimeLimit 'Query exceeded command timeout of 1ms' and no errorLabels (b.1, b.2, b.6-b.9, b2.3, b2.10). It succeeds when the first batch is cheap (b2.5-b2.8). getMores sent without maxTimeMS are not limited (driver_commands show 0 getMores carrying maxTimeMS). Two parts go beyond the evidence. (1) 'The open-source run's find never failed because its first batch was cheap. That is the same per-command behaviour' was not observed on the open-source engine. That engine was never given an expensive first batch (its d.6-d.11 never ran), its d.2 first batch took 2 ms client-side, and ENGINE-TESTS.md calls find enforcement inconclusive. Only a different outcome on different data was observed (200k docs with a 34% match rate vs 50k with 1.7%). (2) The mechanism 'has to work more than about 1 ms to produce its first batch' is inferred, although the conclusion is labelled observed. No real first-batch cost was measured. The 3.5 ms cited for b.1/b.2 comes from an executionStats explain (b2.1) of the bitmap plan, whose leaf IXSCAN returned all 50,000 _id_ keys before fetching. The same kind of explain reported 1.612 ms for find({}) limit 101 (b2.2), yet the real find({}) with maxTimeMS 1 succeeded with batchSize 101 and with 1000 (b2.6, b2.8). Explain time therefore does not measure the real first batch. The indexed-point case (b2.3) also rests on the allPlansExecution and latency inference, not on a measured first-batch cost.

disputed.question: (a) Is COLLSCAN ever shown for the unindexed find?
disputed.reason: The plan observations are right for both states. At allVisibleFraction 0.0, explains with no verbosity, queryPlanner or executionStats show FETCH over a bitmap IXSCAN _id_, and allPlansExecution shows COLLSCAN 'Primary Key Scan'. At 1.0, the first three show a root COLLSCAN with ns and allPlansExecution shows FETCH/IXSCAN 'Primary Key Scan'. Four parts over-reach. (1) vs_open_source 'same' overstates. The open-source engine never showed COLLSCAN for an unindexed find. It was explained only on a freshly loaded collection at executionStats, and its 0.117 explain has no collectionPlannerStatistics, so even its vacuum state is inferred from timing. The vacuumed and allPlansExecution cases that make the managed answer 'yes' were not tested locally, and the report's own per-step verdicts for a5.* say not_tested_locally. The accurate verdict is 'same for the fresh executionStats case, otherwise not tested locally'. (2) 'The first roughly 20-30 s after a 50,000-doc load' turns three bracketed observations into a duration. Run 5 was vacuumed by 20.5 s, possibly as early as 0.2 s. Run 4 changed between 10.7 and 30.8 s. Run 3 still showed 0.0 about 26 s after its 18.8 s load (x3.6 at 21:07:15). Autovacuum scheduling and load on the shared cluster were not observed. (3) The earlier agent run (runs/01-anti-money-laundering-pattern-detector/20261124-200112) matches the vacuumed case only by shape. Its recorded explain in events.jsonl is truncated before allVisibleFraction, so its vacuum state was not observed. (4) Minor: queryPlanner verbosity was never run on the 5,000-doc collection (P4 ran with no verbosity, executionStats and allPlansExecution), and the empty-filter FETCH has no runtimeFilterSet.

extra_observations: Secrets check, nothing redacted and no file modified. Every file under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-julietai-claude/40f65f7c-640c-44c6-8eab-a8434709e1ff/scratchpad/managed-tests/m-query/ was scanned, including __pycache__, for the password and for credentialed mongodb:// URIs. None appear. Password forms checked: raw, quote_plus, quote, JSON-escaped, base64, 12-character prefix and suffix. The az subscription id, tenant id and signed-in account name are absent. The only e-mail-like match was the bytecode string 'buildInfo@client.admin.command' in run.cpython-313.pyc, not an address. The only GUID is the scratchpad session directory name in file paths. Recorded connection options are tls, authMechanism, retrywrites and maxIdleTimeMS only.

Regenerated the seed data locally (no cluster contact). The slow predicate has 861 matches; the first is i=0 (why b2.7's batchSize-1 first batch was trivially cheap) and the 101st is i=5427. rnd>0.999 gives 45 documents and grp=5 gives 516, 52 of them in the first 5,000. i=12345 is the 12,346th document and the first grp=5 document is the 6th. These match the leaf COLLSCAN counts in x3.1 (12,346) and a5.P7 (6). The sorted rnd values match d.1 and d.4.

Vector claim: the scripts never compute exact neighbours or cosine values, yet the conclusion says the top five are exact and the scores equal exact cosine similarities to 6 decimals. Recomputed locally from random.Random(3): the exact top five by cosine are 201, 122, 91, 181, 266. Managed scores are within 4e-8 of the exact values, so the claim is true but unrecorded.

The window tests discriminate less than the conclusions imply, on the managed service and on the open-source engine alike (identical data). c.1 and c.2 compare only final per-partition values (finalTotal, finalMax), which a whole-partition window would also produce. In c.3, runningMax is constantly 15 in the east partition, so cumulative $max is not distinguished there; only runningTotal is. On the L08 data, the exact example c.4 (momentum-1) would return 246/-58 even if the peak window were unbounded. Only c.4b discriminates cumulative $max: meanrev-2 would give 308 instead of 67 and breakout-3 208 instead of 157. Since c.4b matched, the 'yes' answers stand.

allPlansExecution does not always show a streaming-cursor plan. For the limit-1 singleBatch find (x3.1) and the _id lookup (x3.5) there is no cursorScanType, and the plan equals executionStats. On the fresh collection, the limit-1 find's executionStats plan was itself LIMIT over a COLLSCAN carrying indexName _id_ and examining 12,346 documents, despite the i_1 index.

On a just-loaded collection, executionStats counts describe the planner plan, not the cursor plan the real find appears to run. a.3 reports 1/1 on i_1 while allPlansExecution and latency indicate about 50,000 examined. Reading the leaf stage, as the totals conclusion advises, does not fix that case. The verbosity conclusion, correctly labelled inferred, covers it.

estimatedDocumentCount was 94,932 before CREATE INDEX and exactly 50,000 right after it (run1 a.1 vs a.3), with allVisibleFraction still 0.0, so index creation updates the row estimate and only allVisibleFraction tracks the vacuum. After vacuum, indexCosts gain a 'correlation' field and the 5,000-doc collection's estimate went from 9,558 to 5,000, consistent with an ANALYZE in the same pass. Whether the plan flip comes from the visibility map or from the new statistics was not separated.

Latency noise. In run4 M0, the plain indexed find was only +5.7 ms over the _id baseline against +11.7 ms for the full scan, because the baseline median was inflated (samples 70-83 ms). By minimums it is +12.2 vs +14.7 ms. In M1 the hinted find failed 0/3 at maxTimeMS 8 while passing at 1-4 ms. The step-level numbers quoted in the conclusions (run 3 medians and sweeps, run 4 M1) match the raw data.

Drop check: the check_dropped.py result quoted in the conclusion is not saved in any file. A read-only check during this review (list_database_names, then list_collection_names on mt_query) returned mt_query_listed false with no collections. The five runs' own drop steps all record mt_query_still_listed false.

Minor wording: '50,000 docs came back through one getMore' was 101 in the first batch plus 49,899 in one getMore (b2.5). The second case was 1,000 in the first batch plus 49 getMores of 1,000 (b2.8). Also, report.json's drop conclusion lacks the check_dropped sentence that the relayed report contains.

Verified as stated: all quoted codes, codeNames, errmsgs and errorLabels (absent); driver_timeout_property True; the stage-name set across all five runs (COLLSCAN, FETCH, GROUP, GROUPSORT, IXSCAN, LIMIT, PROJECT, PROJECTION_DEFAULT, SORT); the 28-entry $setWindowFields sequence and every other compared explain stage sequence, identical to open-source; top-level key order; explains with no verbosity identical to queryPlanner (T1-T4, A, P1). Also verified: PyMongo 4.20.1 Cursor.explain() sends no verbosity; the $search explain details (nProbes 2, vec_ivf, direction Forward, hasOrderBy true, 5/5) and listIndexes cosmosSearchOptions; the c.1/c.2/c.3/c.6/c.7 documents identical to open-source; L08 values matching an independent recomputation; allowDiskUse timings 216/238/275 ms and the TypeMismatch messages.
summary: The m-query report is accurate at the step level. I read run.py, run2.py-run5.py, finalize.py, probe.py and check_dropped.py, and the five raw reports (report.run1-5.json) next to /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-julietai-claude/40f65f7c-640c-44c6-8eab-a8434709e1ff/scratchpad/managed-tests/m-query/report.json. Every quoted code, codeName, errmsg, stage name, count, latency and maxTimeMS threshold matches the recorded raw responses. Recomputing the seeds locally confirmed the document counts, the window and L08 expected values, and the exact vector neighbours. Most conclusions follow from the data, including the inferred one that the real find follows the allPlansExecution cursor plan and that this changes once the service vacuums the table (correctly labelled inferred). Two conclusions over-reach. (1) The find maxTimeMS conclusion calls the open-source engine 'the same per-command behaviour' and attributes its non-failure to a cheap first batch; neither was observed there. It also presents an explain-derived first-batch cost (3.5 ms, bitmap plan) as the mechanism, while b2.2 vs b2.6/b2.8 show explain time does not predict the real first batch. (2) The COLLSCAN conclusion labels the comparison 'same' although open-source never showed COLLSCAN and its vacuumed and allPlansExecution cases were not tested. It also generalises autovacuum timing ('first roughly 20-30 s') from three bracketed observations. Smaller gaps: the vector exactness check and the check_dropped.py result were not recorded, though both were confirmed during review. The window tests' final-value checks cannot tell cumulative from whole-partition windows; only c.4b distinguishes cumulative $max. No password, credentialed URI, e-mail, subscription, tenant or object id appears in the test directory, so nothing was redacted. The only cluster contact during review was one read-only check, which confirmed mt_query is gone.
